knowledge_gaps: Adjacent-edge counts are used to gate all three recent sources, although older sources require multi-step transition evidence. The counting window, suffix weights, and handling of repeated items need explicit definitions.

Leave-user-out counting requires user identity, but the specified training loader supplies None instead of user IDs. Singleton edges receive no residual training signal yet activate at inference, creating a support-distribution mismatch.

Reproduction requires numerical hyperparameters, initialization, sparse lookup design, and a reliable context-passing contract for diagnosis and inference. Missing these details makes the difficulty rating optimistic.

The evaluation lacks count-only and ungated asymmetric baselines, a concrete GPU-budget allocation, and checks for popularity shortcuts and validation-selection overfitting. Originality also needs comparison with established factorized transition models.

follow_up_queries.reason: Assess novelty and establish simpler controls that distinguish learned asymmetric relationships from transition-count memorization.
follow_up_queries.query: How do FPMC, TransRec, and sparse item-to-item sequential recommenders combine asymmetric transition scores with personalized sequential scores? Compare their formulations with a SASRec residual gated by distinct-user transition counts, including count-only baselines and popularity-normalized transition estimates.

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve the strongest methodological risk: leave-user-out gating can eliminate singleton-edge training while enabling those edges at inference, and the loader lacks user IDs.
follow_up_queries.query: In sequential recommendation with sparse transition-count features, how do leave-one-user-out estimation and user-level cross-fitting prevent target leakage while controlling train-inference feature-distribution mismatch? Investigate treatment of singleton transitions, identity requirements, and direct-adjacent versus multi-step counts when scoring from the latest three items.

follow_up_queries.reason: Determine whether the proposed implementation and validation can reliably isolate gains within the fixed budget.
follow_up_queries.query: What efficient PyTorch designs support batched sparse directed-edge count lookups and bounded candidate-specific residual scoring for SASRec, including chunked full-catalog inference? What paired uncertainty estimates and ablations are appropriate when comparing models on fixed sampled HR@10 with 200 users per category, 99 negatives, four categories, and repeated validation-based model selection?
